questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the complex which exhibits all 3 characteristics; paramagnetic; high spin configuration; octahedral geometry
questions.solution:
In option (A), the complex is $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2$. The central metal ion is $\text{Co}^{3+}$, which has a $3d^6$ configuration. Since $\text{NH}_3$ acts as a strong field ligand for $\text{Co}^{3+}$, it causes pairing of electrons, resulting in a low spin, diamagnetic, and octahedral complex.

In option (B), the complex is $[\text{Ni(CO)}_4]$. The central metal is $\text{Ni}$ in the $0$ oxidation state, with a $3d^{10}$ configuration. It forms an $sp^3$ hybridized, tetrahedral, and diamagnetic complex.

In option (C), the complex is $[\text{Ni(H}_2\text{O})_2(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_2]^{2-}$. The central metal ion is $\text{Ni}^{2+}$, which has a $3d^8$ configuration. The ligands $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ are weak field ligands. The coordination number is $6$ (two from water and four from two bidentate oxalate ions), leading to an octahedral geometry. The $3d^8$ configuration in an octahedral field is $t_{2g}^6 e_g^2$, which has $2$ unpaired electrons. It undergoes $sp^3d^2$ hybridization, forming an outer orbital (high spin) and paramagnetic complex.

In option (D), the complex is $[\text{Co(NH}_3)(\text{Cl})(\text{en})_2]^{2+}$. The central metal ion is $\text{Co}^{3+}$ ($3d^6$). The presence of strong field ligands like ethylenediamine ($\text{en}$) and $\text{NH}_3$ causes electron pairing, resulting in a low spin, diamagnetic, and octahedral complex.

Therefore, only $[\text{Ni(H}_2\text{O})_2(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_2]^{2-}$ exhibits all three characteristics: paramagnetic, high spin configuration, and octahedral geometry.

Answer: $[\text{Ni(H}_2\text{O})_2(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_2]^{2-}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following complex-isomerism pair matches correctly?
options: $[\text{CrCl}_2(ox)_2]^{3-}$ - Exhibits cis- trans isomerism and cis isomer is optically active
$[\text{PtCl}_2(\text{NH}_3)_2]$ - Exhibits both cis- trans and optical isomerism
$[\text{Cr(C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]^{3-}$ - Exhibits cis- trans isomerism but is optically inactive
$[\text{Fe(CN)}_4(\text{NH}_3)_2]^-$ - Exhibits cis- trans isomerism and both exhibit optical isomerism
questions.solution:
$[\text{CrCl}_2(ox)_2]^{3-}$ is an octahedral complex of the type $[M(AA)_2a_2]$. It exhibits geometrical isomerism, existing as cis and trans isomers.

The trans isomer has a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive.

The cis isomer lacks any plane or center of symmetry and is optically active, existing as a pair of enantiomers.

$[\text{PtCl}_2(\text{NH}_3)_2]$ is a square planar complex of the type $[Ma_2b_2]$. It exhibits geometrical isomerism (cis and trans) but is optically inactive due to the presence of a molecular plane of symmetry.

$[\text{Cr(C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]^{3-}$ is an octahedral complex of the type $[M(AA)_3]$. It does not exhibit geometrical isomerism but is optically active.

$[\text{Fe(CN)}_4(\text{NH}_3)_2]^-$ is an octahedral complex of the type $[Ma_4b_2]$. It exhibits geometrical isomerism (cis and trans), but both isomers possess a plane of symmetry and are optically inactive.

Answer: $[\text{CrCl}_2(ox)_2]^{3-}$ - Exhibits cis- trans isomerism and cis isomer is optically active

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match the Coordination compounds in Column I with the type of stereoisomerism given in Column II exhibited by them.
Column IColumn II
A. $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$P. fac-mer
B. $\text{Ni}[(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$Q. cis-trans
C. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_3(\text{NO}_2)_3]$R. only cis isomer shows optical isomerism
D. $[\text{Pt}\,\text{Cl}_2(\text{en})_2]^{2+}$S. does not exhibit isomerism.
options: A - Q B - S C - P D - R
A - R B - P C - S D - Q
A - S B - P C - Q D - R
A - S B - R C - Q D - P
questions.solution:
$[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$ is a square planar complex of the type $MA_2B_2$. It exhibits cis-trans isomerism. This matches Q.

$[\text{Ni}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$ is a tetrahedral complex of the type $MA_2B_2$ since $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ is a $3d^8$ ion and forms $sp^3$ hybridized complexes with weak field ligands. Tetrahedral complexes do not exhibit geometrical isomerism, and since it lacks four different ligands, it does not show optical isomerism. Thus, it does not exhibit isomerism. This matches S.

$[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_3(\text{NO}_2)_3]$ is an octahedral complex of the type $MA_3B_3$. It exhibits facial (fac) and meridional (mer) isomerism. This matches P.

$[\text{PtCl}_2(\text{en})_2]^{2+}$ is an octahedral complex of the type $M(AA)_2B_2$. It exhibits cis-trans isomerism. The cis isomer lacks a plane of symmetry and is optically active, while the trans isomer has a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive. This matches R.

Therefore, A matches Q, B matches S, C matches P, and D matches R.

Answer: A - Q B - S C - P D - R

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The Crystal Field Stabilisation energy of (i) $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$ and (ii) $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ are ----- and ------- respectively.
questions.solution:
For the complex $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$:
The oxidation state of Co is $+3$. The electronic configuration of $\text{Co}^{3+}$ is $3d^6$.
Since $\text{F}^-$ is a weak field ligand, the complex is high-spin. The electrons are distributed in the $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ orbitals as $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$.
$\text{CFSE} = (-0.4 \times n_{t_{2g}} + 0.6 \times n_{e_g}) \Delta_0$
$\text{CFSE} = (-0.4 \times 4 + 0.6 \times 2) \Delta_0 = (-1.6 + 1.2) \Delta_0 = -0.4 \Delta_0$

For the complex $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$:
The oxidation state of Fe is $+3$. The electronic configuration of $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ is $3d^5$.
Since $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is a weak field ligand, the complex is high-spin. The electrons are distributed as $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$.
$\text{CFSE} = (-0.4 \times 3 + 0.6 \times 2) \Delta_0 = (-1.2 + 1.2) \Delta_0 = 0 \Delta_0$

Answer: (i) $-0.4\Delta_0$ (ii) $0\ \Delta_0$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of geometrical isomers in the following metal complexes $\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_4,\left[\mathrm{Ru}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_3 \mathrm{Cl}_3\right],\left[\mathrm{CuCl}_2\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4\right]^{+}$and $\left[\mathrm{PtCl}_2\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_2\right]$ are
questions.solution:
The complex $\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_4$ is a tetrahedral complex of the type $MA_4$. Tetrahedral complexes of the type $MA_4$ or $MA_3B$ do not exhibit geometrical isomerism. Thus, the number of geometrical isomers is $0$.

The complex $[\mathrm{Ru}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_3\mathrm{Cl}_3]$ is an octahedral complex of the type $MA_3B_3$. This type of complex exhibits two geometrical isomers: the facial (fac) isomer and the meridional (mer) isomer. Thus, the number of geometrical isomers is $2$.

The complex $[\mathrm{CuCl}_2(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4]^{+}$ is an octahedral complex of the type $MA_4B_2$. This type of complex exhibits two geometrical isomers: the trans isomer (where the two Cl ligands are at $180^{\circ}$) and the cis isomer (where the two Cl ligands are at $90^{\circ}$). Thus, the number of geometrical isomers is $2$.

The complex $[\mathrm{PtCl}_2(\mathrm{NH}_3)_2]$ is a square planar complex of the type $MA_2B_2$. This type of complex exhibits two geometrical isomers: the cis isomer and the trans isomer. Thus, the number of geometrical isomers is $2$.

The sequence of the number of geometrical isomers is $0, 2, 2, 2$.

Answer: $0,2,2,2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The wavelength absorbed by the complex $[Cu(H_2O)_4]^{2+}$ (assuming tetrahedral geometry) for the d-d transition is 600 nm. The crystal field splitting energy for the complex $[Cu(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$ is:
[Given: $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\text{ Js}$, $c = 3 \times 10^8\text{ ms}^{-1}$, and $1\text{ eV} = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}$]
questions.solution:
Tetrahedral splitting energy:

$\Delta_t = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} = \dfrac{(6.626 \times 10^{-34})(3 \times 10^8)}{600 \times 10^{-9}} = 3.313 \times 10^{-19}$ J

Since $\Delta_t = \dfrac{4}{9}\Delta_o$:

$\Delta_o = \dfrac{9}{4} \times 3.313 \times 10^{-19} = 7.454 \times 10^{-19}$ J

Converting to eV:

$\Delta_o = \dfrac{7.454 \times 10^{-19}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}} \approx 4.7$ eV

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The 'd' electronic configuration of $\left[\mathrm{Ru}(\mathrm{en})_3\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2$ and $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_6\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2$ respectively are _____ and ____ .
[Given: Atomic number of $\mathrm{Ru}=44$ and $\mathrm{Fe}=26$ ]
questions.solution:
For $\left[\mathrm{Ru}(\mathrm{en})_3\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2$, the oxidation state of $\mathrm{Ru}$ is $+2$. The atomic number of $\mathrm{Ru}$ is $44$, so its electronic configuration is $[\mathrm{Kr}] 4d^7 5s^1$. For $\mathrm{Ru}^{2+}$, the configuration is $4d^6$. Since $\mathrm{Ru}$ is a $4d$ transition metal, it forms low-spin complexes regardless of the ligand field strength. Thus, the $d^6$ configuration in an octahedral field results in $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$.

For $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2$, the oxidation state of $\mathrm{Fe}$ is $+2$. The atomic number of $\mathrm{Fe}$ is $26$, so its electronic configuration is $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^6 4s^2$. For $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$, the configuration is $3d^6$. Since $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ is a weak field ligand, the complex is high-spin. The $d^6$ configuration in a high-spin octahedral field is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$.

Therefore, the configurations are $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$ and $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$.

Answer: $t_{2 g}{ }^6 e_g^0 ; t_{2 g}{ }^4 e_g^2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A transition metal M forms 4 homoleptic octahedral coordination compounds, A, B, C and D of the type [MX6] ${ }^{z-}$ with monodentate ligands $\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c}$ and d respectively. These compounds absorb red, blue, yellow and blue-green light respectively. Which one of the options shows the correct order of decreasing ligand strength?
questions.solution:
The energy of the absorbed light is inversely proportional to the wavelength of the light absorbed, given by $E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$.

The crystal field splitting energy $\Delta_o$ is directly proportional to the energy of the absorbed light. Therefore, $\Delta_o \propto \dfrac{1}{\lambda}$.

The wavelengths of the colors are approximately: Yellow (570-590 nm) < Red (620-750 nm) < Blue-Green (490-500 nm) < Blue (450-495 nm).

The absorbed colors are given as: A (Red), B (Blue), C (Yellow), D (Blue-Green).

The wavelengths follow the order: $\lambda_{Red} \gt \lambda_{Yellow} \gt \lambda_{Blue-Green} \gt \lambda_{Blue}$.

Since $\Delta_o$ is inversely proportional to $\lambda$, the order of $\Delta_o$ (and thus ligand strength) is: $\Delta_{o, Blue} \gt \Delta_{o, Blue-Green} \gt \Delta_{o, Yellow} \gt \Delta_{o, Red}$.

Substituting the compounds: B > D > C > A.

Answer: $\mathrm{B}\gt \mathrm{D}\gt \mathrm{C}\gt \mathrm{A}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The correct order of spin only magnetic moments among the following is:
[Given: Atomic numbers: $\mathrm{Mn}=25, \mathrm{Fe}=26, \mathrm{Co}=27$ ]
questions.solution:
For $\left[\mathrm{MnCl}_4\right]^{2-}$: Mn is in $+2$ oxidation state ($d^5$ configuration). Since $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, the electrons remain unpaired. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 5$. Magnetic moment $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{5(7)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92$ BM.

For $\left[\mathrm{CoCl}_4\right]^{2-}$: Co is in $+2$ oxidation state ($d^7$ configuration). Since $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, the electrons remain unpaired. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 3$. Magnetic moment $\mu = \sqrt{3(5)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87$ BM.

For $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$: Fe is in $+2$ oxidation state ($d^6$ configuration). Since $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$ is a strong field ligand, it causes pairing of electrons. All $6$ electrons pair up in the $t_{2g}$ orbitals. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 0$. Magnetic moment $\mu = 0$ BM.

Comparing the values: $5.92 \gt 3.87 \gt 0$. Therefore, the order is $\left[\mathrm{MnCl}_4\right]^{2-} \gt \left[\mathrm{CoCl}_4\right]^{2-} \gt \left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{MnCl}_4\right]^{2-}\gt \left[\mathrm{CoCl}_4\right]^{2-}\gt \left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the coordination compound which does not exhibit Optical activity.
questions.solution:
Optical activity in coordination compounds requires the absence of a plane of symmetry and a center of inversion.

The complex $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_3\right]^{3+}$ is a tris-chelated octahedral complex which lacks both a plane of symmetry and a center of inversion, hence it is optically active.

The complex cis $-\left[\mathrm{CoCl}_2(\mathrm{en})_2\right]^{+}$ lacks a plane of symmetry and a center of inversion, making it optically active.

The complex cis $-\left[\mathrm{PtCl}_2(\mathrm{en})_2\right]^{2+}$ also lacks a plane of symmetry and a center of inversion, making it optically active.

The complex trans $-\left[\mathrm{CoCl}_2(\mathrm{en})_2\right]^{+}$ possesses a plane of symmetry (the equatorial plane containing the metal and the two chlorine atoms) and a center of inversion. Therefore, it is achiral and does not exhibit optical activity.

Answer: trans $-\left[\mathrm{CoCl}_2(\mathrm{en})_2\right]^{+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which one of the following structures in Column I does not have the correct IUPAC name as given in Column II.
\(\begin{array}{|c|l|l|} \hline \text { S.No. } & \text { Structure } & \text { IUPAC name. } \\ \hline \text { A } & {\left[\mathrm{CoBr} r_2(\mathrm{en})_2\right] \mathrm{Cl}} & \text { Dibromidodi-( ethan-1, 2 - diamine)cobalt (III) chloride } \\ \hline \text { B } & \mathrm{Na}\left[\mathrm{PtBrCl}\left(\mathrm{NO}_2\right)\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)\right] & \text { Sodium amminebromidochloridonitrito- N- palatinate(II) } \\ \hline \text { C } & {\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_2\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4 \mathrm{Cl}\right] \mathrm{SO}_4} & \text { Tetraamminediaquachloridochromium (III) sulphate. } \\ \hline \text { D } & {\left[\mathrm{Pt}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4\right]\left[\mathrm{PtCl}_4\right]} & \text { Tetraammineplatinum (II) tetrachloridoplatinate (II) } \\ \hline \end{array}\)
questions.solution:
In option A, the complex is $\left[\mathrm{CoBr}_{2}(\mathrm{en})_{2}\right]\mathrm{Cl}$. The IUPAC name is dibromidobis(ethane-1,2-diamine)cobalt(III) chloride. The prefix 'di' is used for simple ligands, but for ligands like ethane-1,2-diamine which already contain a numerical prefix, 'bis' should be used. Thus, the name given in the table is incorrect.

In option B, the complex is $\mathrm{Na}\left[\mathrm{PtBrCl}(\mathrm{NO}_{2})(\mathrm{NH}_{3})\right]$. The ligands are ammine, bromido, chlorido, and nitrito-N. Alphabetical order is ammine, bromido, chlorido, nitrito-N. The metal is in the anion, so it is platinate(II). The name sodium amminebromidochloridonitrito-N-platinate(II) is correct.

In option C, the complex is $\left[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{2}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{4}\mathrm{Cl}\right]\mathrm{SO}_{4}$. The ligands are tetraammine, diaqua, chlorido. Alphabetical order is ammine, aqua, chlorido. The name tetraamminediaquachloridochromium(III) sulphate is correct.

In option D, the complex is $\left[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{4}\right]\left[\mathrm{PtCl}_{4}\right]$. The cation is tetraammineplatinum(II) and the anion is tetrachloridoplatinate(II). The name is correct.

Answer: A

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the coordination compounds [(i) to (v)] are used for the following processes:

C: Estimation of hardness of water

 (iv) D-penicillamine  (v) $\mathrm{K}\left[\mathrm{Au}(\mathrm{CN})_2\right]$

The coordination compound $\mathrm{K}[\mathrm{Au}(\mathrm{CN})_2]$ (v) is used in the electroplating of gold. Therefore, A = v.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds has electrons symmetrically distributed in both $\mathrm{t}_{2 \mathrm{~g}}$ and eg orbitals?
questions.solution:
The electronic configuration of the central metal ion in each complex is determined as follows:

For $\left[\mathrm{CoF}_6\right]^{3-}$, the oxidation state of Co is $+3$. The configuration of $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ is $3d^6$. Since $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, the configuration is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$. The distribution is not symmetric.

For $\left[\mathrm{FeCl}_6\right]^{3-}$, the oxidation state of Fe is $+3$. The configuration of $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ is $3d^5$. Since $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, the configuration is $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$. The distribution is symmetric as $t_{2g}$ is half-filled ($3$ electrons) and $e_g$ is half-filled ($2$ electrons).

For $\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$, the oxidation state of Cr is $+3$. The configuration of $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ is $3d^3$. The configuration is $t_{2g}^3 e_g^0$. The distribution is not symmetric.

For $\left[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$, the oxidation state of Mn is $+2$. The configuration of $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ is $3d^5$. Since $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$ is a strong field ligand, the configuration is $t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$. The distribution is not symmetric.

Thus, $\left[\mathrm{FeCl}_6\right]^{3-}$ has a symmetric distribution of electrons in both $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ orbitals.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{FeCl}_6\right]^{3-}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Arrange the complex ions in the increasing order of their magnetic moments
A. $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$
B. $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$
C. $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-}$
D. $\left[\mathrm{FeF}_6\right]^{3-}$
questions.solution:
The magnetic moment is calculated using the formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ B.M., where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

A. In $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6\right]^{2+}$, Fe is in $+2$ oxidation state ($3d^6$). $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ is a weak field ligand, so electrons remain unpaired: $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 4$. $\mu = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90$ B.M.

B. In $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$, Fe is in $+2$ oxidation state ($3d^6$). $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$ is a strong field ligand, causing pairing: $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 0$. $\mu = 0$ B.M.

C. In $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-}$, Fe is in $+3$ oxidation state ($3d^5$). $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$ is a strong field ligand, causing pairing: $t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 1$. $\mu = \sqrt{1(1+2)} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73$ B.M.

D. In $\left[\mathrm{FeF}_6\right]^{3-}$, Fe is in $+3$ oxidation state ($3d^5$). $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, so electrons remain unpaired: $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 5$. $\mu = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92$ B.M.

Comparing the magnetic moments: $0 \lt 1.73 \lt 4.90 \lt 5.92$, which corresponds to $\mathrm{B} \lt \mathrm{C} \lt \mathrm{A} \lt \mathrm{D}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{B} \lt \mathrm{C} \lt \mathrm{A} \lt \mathrm{D}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aqueous solution of $\mathrm{CrCl}_3 .6 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ (Molar mass $=266.5 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}$ ) containing 2.665 g of the solute after processing, when treated with excess of $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ gave 2.87 g of AgCl (Molar mass of $\mathrm{AgCl}=143.5 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}$ ) Choose the correct formula of the compound which give these results.
questions.solution:
The number of moles of the complex $\mathrm{CrCl}_3 \cdot 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ is calculated as:
Moles of complex $= \dfrac{2.665 \text{ g}}{266.5 \text{ g/mol}} = 0.01 \text{ mol}$.

The number of moles of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ precipitated is calculated as:
Moles of $\mathrm{AgCl} = \dfrac{2.87 \text{ g}}{143.5 \text{ g/mol}} = 0.02 \text{ mol}$.

The reaction with $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ precipitates only the chloride ions present outside the coordination sphere. Let $x$ be the number of ionizable chloride ions per mole of the complex. The stoichiometry of the reaction is:
Moles of $\mathrm{AgCl} = x \times \text{Moles of complex}$
$0.02 = x \times 0.01$
$x = 2$.

Since there are 2 ionizable chloride ions, the formula must contain 2 chloride ions outside the coordination sphere. Among the given options, $\left[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_5\mathrm{Cl}\right]\mathrm{Cl}_2 \cdot \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ satisfies this condition.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_5 \mathrm{Cl}\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2 \cdot \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following coordination compounds will exhibit both geometrical and optical isomerism?
questions.solution:
The complex $\left[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{ox})_3\right]^{3-}$ is a tris-chelated complex of the form $M(AA)_3$. It exhibits optical isomerism but does not show geometrical isomerism because all donor atoms are identical.

The complex $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-}$ is an octahedral complex of the form $MA_6$. It does not exhibit either geometrical or optical isomerism.

The complex $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_2 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right]^{+}$ is of the form $M(AA)_2 a_2$. The cis-isomer of this complex is optically active (chiral) and also exists as a geometrical isomer (cis and trans). The trans-isomer is optically inactive due to the presence of a plane of symmetry. Since the cis-isomer exhibits both geometrical (relative to trans) and optical isomerism, this complex satisfies the condition.

The complex $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NO}_3)_3(\mathrm{NH}_3)_3\right]$ is of the form $Ma_3b_3$. It exhibits geometrical isomerism (fac and mer isomers) but does not exhibit optical isomerism as both isomers possess planes of symmetry.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_2 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right]^{+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Arrange the following compounds in the decreasing order of the molar conductivities of their aqueous solutions.
$\begin{array}{cccc}\mathrm{A} & \quad \mathrm{B} & \quad \mathrm{C} & \quad \mathrm{D} \\ {\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5 \mathrm{Cl}] \mathrm{Cl}_2\right.} & \quad {\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_3 \mathrm{Cl}_3\right]} & \quad {\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right] \mathrm{Cl}} & \quad {\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right] \mathrm{Cl}_3}\end{array}$
questions.solution:
Molar conductivity of an electrolyte in aqueous solution depends on the number of ions produced upon dissociation. The greater the number of ions, the higher the molar conductivity.

Dissociation of the given complexes:
A: $[Co(NH_3)_5Cl]Cl_2 \rightarrow [Co(NH_3)_5Cl]^{2+} + 2Cl^{-}$. Total ions = 3.
B: $[Co(NH_3)_3Cl_3] \rightarrow [Co(NH_3)_3Cl_3]$. Total ions = 0 (non-electrolyte).
C: $[Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2]Cl \rightarrow [Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2]^{+} + Cl^{-}$. Total ions = 2.
D: $[Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3 \rightarrow [Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+} + 3Cl^{-}$. Total ions = 4.

Comparing the number of ions produced:
D (4 ions) > A (3 ions) > C (2 ions) > B (0 ions).

Therefore, the decreasing order of molar conductivity is D > A > C > B.

Answer: $D\gt A\gt C\gt B$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match the coordination compounds in Column I having the given type of hybridisation of $\mathrm{M}^{\mathrm{n}+}$ ion and magnetic moment as given in Column II.
\(\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|} \hline & \text { Coordination compounds. } & & \text { Hybridisation \& Magnetic nature. } \\ \hline \text { A } & \mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_4 & \text { P } & \mathrm{sp}^3, \quad \mu=5.92 \mathrm{BM} \\ \hline \text { B } & {\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]^{2-}} & \text { Q } & \mathrm{sp}^3, \quad \mu=2.84 \mathrm{BM} \\ \hline \text { C } & {\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{Cl})_4\right]^{2-}} & \text { R } & \mathrm{sp}^3, \quad \mu=0 \\ \hline \text { D } & {[\mathrm{MnBr}]^{2-}} & \text { S } & \mathrm{dsp}^2, \quad \mu=0 \\ \hline \end{array}\)
questions.solution:
For $\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$, the oxidation state of Ni is 0. The electronic configuration is $[Ar] 3d^8 4s^2$. Since CO is a strong field ligand, it causes pairing of electrons, leading to $sp^3$ hybridization. All electrons are paired, so $\mu = 0$. This matches R.

For $[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}$, the oxidation state of Ni is +2. The electronic configuration is $[Ar] 3d^8$. CN$^-$ is a strong field ligand, causing pairing of electrons in the $3d$ orbitals, resulting in $dsp^2$ hybridization. All electrons are paired, so $\mu = 0$. This matches S.

For $[Ni(Cl)_4]^{2-}$, the oxidation state of Ni is +2. The electronic configuration is $[Ar] 3d^8$. Cl$^-$ is a weak field ligand, so no pairing occurs. The hybridization is $sp^3$ with two unpaired electrons. The magnetic moment is $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{2(2+2)} = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.84$ BM. This matches Q.

For $[MnBr_4]^{2-}$, the oxidation state of Mn is +2. The electronic configuration is $[Ar] 3d^5$. Br$^-$ is a weak field ligand, so no pairing occurs. The hybridization is $sp^3$ with five unpaired electrons. The magnetic moment is $\mu = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92$ BM. This matches P.

Answer: $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{R} \quad \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{S} \quad \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{Q} \quad \mathrm{D}=\mathrm{P}$

questions.q: The type of hybridisation and the spin only magnetic moment for the complex $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_4]$ are respectively:
questions.solution:
The central metal atom is Nickel (Ni) with atomic number 28. The electronic configuration of Ni is $[Ar] 3d^{8} 4s^{2}$.

In the complex $[Ni(CO)_{4}]$, the oxidation state of Ni is 0, as CO is a neutral ligand. The configuration remains $[Ar] 3d^{8} 4s^{2}$.

CO is a strong field ligand, which causes the pairing of electrons in the $3d$ orbital. The two electrons from the $4s$ orbital are promoted to the $3d$ orbital to complete the $3d^{10}$ configuration, leaving the $4s$ and $4p$ orbitals vacant.

The four CO ligands donate electron pairs into one $4s$ and three $4p$ orbitals, resulting in $sp^{3}$ hybridization. This leads to a tetrahedral geometry.

Since all electrons are paired in the $3d^{10}$ configuration, the number of unpaired electrons $n = 0$. The spin only magnetic moment $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{0(0+2)} = 0 \text{ BM}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{sp}^3$, zero

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The molar conductivity of the complex $\mathrm{CoCl}_3 \cdot 4 \mathrm{NH}_3 \cdot 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ is found to be the same as that of a $1: 3$ electrolyte. The structural formula of the compound is :
questions.solution:
The molar conductivity of a $1:3$ electrolyte indicates that the complex dissociates into $4$ ions in total, consisting of one complex cation and three chloride anions. This implies that all three chloride ions are present outside the coordination sphere as counter ions.

The coordination number of Cobalt in such complexes is typically $6$. The formula given is $\mathrm{CoCl}_3 \cdot 4 \mathrm{NH}_3 \cdot 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$.

If the complex is a $1:3$ electrolyte, the structure must be of the form $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O})_2]\mathrm{Cl}_3$. In this structure, the coordination sphere contains $4$ ammonia molecules and $2$ water molecules, satisfying the coordination number of $6$. The three chloride ions are outside the coordination sphere, which leads to the dissociation: $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O})_2]\mathrm{Cl}_3 \rightarrow [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O})_2]^{3+} + 3\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$.

This confirms the complex is a $1:3$ electrolyte.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_2\right] \mathrm{Cl}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: On the basis of crystal field theory, electronic configuration of a low spin $\mathrm{d}^4$ complex is:
questions.solution:
In an octahedral crystal field, the d-orbitals split into two sets: the lower energy $t_{2g}$ set and the higher energy $e_g$ set.

For a $d^4$ metal ion in a low spin complex, the crystal field splitting energy $\Delta_o$ is greater than the pairing energy $P$.

According to the Aufbau principle and Hund's rule, electrons fill the lower energy $t_{2g}$ orbitals first. Since the complex is low spin, pairing occurs in the $t_{2g}$ orbitals before any electrons occupy the $e_g$ orbitals.

For a $d^4$ configuration, the first three electrons occupy the $t_{2g}$ orbitals singly. The fourth electron pairs up in one of the $t_{2g}$ orbitals because $\Delta_o \gt P$.

Therefore, the electronic configuration is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^0$.

Answer: $t_{2 g}^4 e_g$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following 2 compounds exhibit both Geometrical and Structural isomerism?
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{A}=\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right] \mathrm{NO}_2 \\
& \mathrm{~B}=\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right) \mathrm{Br}\right] \mathrm{SO}_4 \\
& \mathrm{C}=\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_3\left(\mathrm{NO}_2\right)_3\right] \\
& \mathrm{D}=\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_6\right] \mathrm{Cl}_3
\end{aligned}$
questions.solution:
Compound A is $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right] \mathrm{NO}_2$. It exhibits structural isomerism (ionization isomerism with $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4 \mathrm{Cl} \mathrm{NO}_2\right] \mathrm{Cl}$) and geometrical isomerism (cis and trans forms of the $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right]^{+}$ ion).

Compound B is $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5 \mathrm{Br}\right] \mathrm{SO}_4$. It exhibits ionization isomerism with $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5 \mathrm{SO}_4\right] \mathrm{Br}$, but it does not exhibit geometrical isomerism because the coordination sphere $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_5 \mathrm{Br}\right]^{2+}$ is of the type $MA_5B$, which cannot show geometrical isomerism.

Compound C is $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_3\left(\mathrm{NO}_2\right)_3\right]$. It exhibits geometrical isomerism (facial and meridional isomers). It also exhibits linkage isomerism due to the ambidentate ligand $\mathrm{NO}_2^{-}$, which is a type of structural isomerism.

Compound D is $\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_6\right] \mathrm{Cl}_3$. It does not exhibit geometrical isomerism (type $MA_6$) nor structural isomerism (other than hydrate isomerism, which is not possible here as all water molecules are coordinated).

Therefore, compounds A and C exhibit both geometrical and structural isomerism.

Answer: A & C

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are 4 statements. Two of these are correct statements. Identify them.
A. $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$ is easily oxidised to $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ in the presence of a strong ligand like $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$
B. $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{4-}$ is an octahedral complex ion which is paramagnetic in nature.
C. Removal of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ molecules from $[\mathrm{Ti}(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O})_6] \mathrm{Cl}_3$ on strong heating converts it to a colourless compound.
D. Crystal Field splitting in Octahedral and Tetrahedral complexes is given by the equation $\Delta_0=4 / 9 \Delta_t$
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct. In the presence of strong field ligands like $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$, the crystal field splitting energy is high, which stabilizes the $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ oxidation state ($d^6$ configuration) over $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$ ($d^7$ configuration) due to the large crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE).

Statement B is incorrect. $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{4-}$ contains $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ ($d^6$). $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$ is a strong field ligand, causing pairing of electrons in the $t_{2g}$ orbitals. Thus, it is diamagnetic, not paramagnetic.

Statement C is correct. $[\mathrm{Ti}(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O})_6] \mathrm{Cl}_3$ is a $d^1$ complex which is violet in color. Upon strong heating, the water ligands are removed to form anhydrous $\mathrm{TiCl}_3$, which is colorless as the $d-d$ transition is no longer possible in the absence of the ligand field.

Statement D is incorrect. The relationship between octahedral splitting ($\Delta_0$) and tetrahedral splitting ($\Delta_t$) is given by $\Delta_t = \dfrac{4}{9} \Delta_0$, or $\Delta_0 = \dfrac{9}{4} \Delta_t$.

Answer: A & C

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A d - block metal $\mathrm{X}(\mathrm{Z}=26)$ forms a compound $[\mathrm{X}(\mathrm{CN})_2(\mathrm{CO})_4]^{+}$. Calculate its spin magnetic moment value.
questions.solution:
The metal X is Iron (Fe) with atomic number $Z = 26$. The electronic configuration of Fe is $[Ar] 3d^{6} 4s^{2}$.

In the complex $[Fe(CN)_{2}(CO)_{4}]^{+}$, let the oxidation state of Fe be $x$. Since $CN^{-}$ is $-1$ and $CO$ is neutral, we have $x + 2(-1) + 4(0) = +1$, which gives $x = +3$.

The electronic configuration of $Fe^{3+}$ is $[Ar] 3d^{5}$.

Both $CN^{-}$ and $CO$ are strong field ligands. According to crystal field theory, strong field ligands cause pairing of electrons in the $d$-orbitals. For a $d^{5}$ configuration with strong field ligands, the electrons pair up in the $t_{2g}$ orbitals: $(t_{2g})^{5} (e_{g})^{0}$.

The number of unpaired electrons $n = 1$.

The spin magnetic moment $\mu$ is calculated using the formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM. Substituting $n = 1$, we get $\mu = \sqrt{1(1+2)} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73$ BM.

Answer: 1.73 BM

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A Coordination compound is represented by the formula $[\mathrm{CoBr}_3(e n) x]$. This compound required one mole of $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ to form a pale yellow precipitate of $\mathrm{AgBr}$. What is the value of $\mathrm{x}$ in the compound?
questions.solution:
The coordination compound is given as $[CoBr_3(en)x]$. The reaction with $AgNO_3$ produces a pale yellow precipitate of $AgBr$, which indicates that one bromide ion is present outside the coordination sphere as a counter ion.

The reaction can be represented as $[CoBr_2(en)x]Br + AgNO_3 \rightarrow [CoBr_2(en)x]NO_3 + AgBr(s)$.

The coordination number of Cobalt(III) in such complexes is typically 6. The ethylenediamine (en) ligand is bidentate, occupying 2 coordination sites. Let the number of bromide ions inside the coordination sphere be $y$. Then the total coordination number is $2(en) + y(Br) = 6$.

Since there are 3 bromide ions in total and 1 is outside, $y = 2$. Thus, $2(en) + 2(Br) = 6$, which implies $2(2) + 2 = 6$. This is consistent with the coordination number of 6.

The formula is $[CoBr_2(en)x]Br$. Comparing this with the given formula $[CoBr_3(en)x]$, we see that $x$ represents the number of ethylenediamine ligands. Since $2(en)$ is required to satisfy the coordination number, $x = 2$.

Answer: 2

questions.solution:
In a tetrahedral complex of the type $[Ma_2b_2]$, all positions are equivalent relative to each other, meaning there is no distinction between cis and trans positions. Thus, it does not show geometrical isomerism. This statement is correct.

For a coordination entity of the type $[Ma_2(bb)_2]^{2+}$, where $(bb)$ is a symmetrical bidentate ligand, the cis-isomer lacks a plane of symmetry and is optically active, while the trans-isomer possesses a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive. This statement is correct.

Coordination entities of the type $[Ma_3b_3]$ exhibit facial (fac) and meridional (mer) geometrical isomers. Therefore, the statement that they do not exhibit geometrical isomerism is incorrect.

A square planar complex of the type $[Mabcd]$ has three possible geometrical isomers, which are obtained by fixing one ligand and arranging the others in different positions relative to it. This statement is correct.

Answer: Coordination entities of the type $[\mathrm{Ma}_3 \mathrm{b}_3]$ do not exhibit geometrical isomerism

Facial (fac) and Meridional (mer) isomerism is a type of geometric isomerism observed in octahedral complexes of the type $[MA_3B_3]$.

In the complex $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_3\left(\mathrm{NO}_2\right)_3\right]$, the central metal ion Co is coordinated to three water ligands and three nitrite ligands. This corresponds to the general formula $[MA_3B_3]$.

When the three identical ligands occupy the corners of one triangular face of the octahedron, it is called the facial (fac) isomer. When the three identical ligands occupy positions around the meridian of the octahedron, it is called the meridional (mer) isomer.

The other options provided are not of the $[MA_3B_3]$ type. $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4 \mathrm{Br}_2\right] \mathrm{NO}_3$ is of the type $[MA_4B_2]$, which exhibits cis-trans isomerism. $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\text { en })_2 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right]^{+}$ is of the type $[M(AA)_2B_2]$, which also exhibits cis-trans isomerism. $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\text { en })_3\right] \mathrm{Cl}_3$ is of the type $[M(AA)_3]$, which exhibits optical isomerism.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_3\left(\mathrm{NO}_2\right)_3\right]$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct IUPAC name of $[\mathrm{CoCl}_2(\mathrm{NO}_2)(\mathrm{NH}_3)_3]$
questions.solution:
The coordination compound is $[CoCl_{2}(NO_{2})(NH_{3})_{3}]$.

First, determine the oxidation state of the central metal atom, Cobalt (Co). Let the oxidation state be $x$. The ligands are $Cl^{-}$ (charge -1), $NO_{2}^{-}$ (charge -1), and $NH_{3}$ (neutral, charge 0). The complex is neutral, so the sum of charges is zero: $x + 2(-1) + 1(-1) + 3(0) = 0$, which gives $x - 3 = 0$, so $x = +3$.

Next, name the ligands in alphabetical order. The ligands are ammine ($NH_{3}$), chlorido ($Cl^{-}$), and nitrito-N ($NO_{2}^{-}$).

There are three ammine ligands, so use the prefix 'tri'. There are two chlorido ligands, so use the prefix 'di'. The ligand $NO_{2}$ is bonded through nitrogen, so it is named 'nitrito-N'.

Combining these, the alphabetical order is ammine, chlorido, nitrito-N. Thus, the name is triamminedichloridonitrito-N-cobalt(III).

Answer: Triamminedichloridonitrito- $\mathrm{N}-\operatorname{cobalt}(\mathrm{III})$

For W: $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5 \mathrm{Cl}\right] \mathrm{Cl}_2$ : Co is in $+3$ oxidation state. $Co^{3+}$ is $d^6$. With strong field ligands like $\mathrm{NH}_3$, it forms a low spin complex with $\mu = 0$ BM. This corresponds to R.

For X: $\mathrm{K}_4\left[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]$. Mn is in $+2$ oxidation state. $Mn^{2+}$ is $d^5$. $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$ is a strong field ligand, causing pairing, resulting in one unpaired electron ($t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$). $\mu = \sqrt{1(1+2)} = 1.732$ BM. This corresponds to S.

For Y: $\left[\mathrm{CrCl}_3(\mathrm{py})_3\right]$. Cr is in $+3$ oxidation state. $Cr^{3+}$ is $d^3$. In octahedral geometry, $t_{2g}^3 e_g^0$, three unpaired electrons. $\mu = \sqrt{3(3+2)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87$ BM. This corresponds to Q.

For Z: $\mathrm{Cs}\left[\mathrm{FeCl}_4\right]$. Fe is in $+3$ oxidation state. $Fe^{3+}$ is $d^5$. $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, forming a high spin tetrahedral complex. Five unpaired electrons, $\mu = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92$ BM. This corresponds to P.

questions.q: Aqueous $\mathrm{CuSO}_4$ changes its colour from sky blue to deep blue on addition of $\mathrm{NH}_3$ because
options: $\left[\mathrm{Cu}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_4\right]^{2+}$ is labile complex and changes to $\left[\mathrm{Cu}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4\right]^{2+}$ as $\mathrm{NH}_3$ is stronger ligand than $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
questions.solution:
Aqueous copper(II) sulfate exists as the complex ion $\left[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_4\right]^{2+}$ (or more accurately $\left[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6\right]^{2+}$), which is sky blue in color.

Upon the addition of ammonia ($\mathrm{NH}_3$), the ammonia molecules act as stronger ligands than water molecules and displace them from the coordination sphere of the copper(II) ion.

The reaction is represented as $\left[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_4\right]^{2+} + 4\mathrm{NH}_3 \rightarrow \left[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4\right]^{2+} + 4\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$.

The resulting complex $\left[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4\right]^{2+}$ (tetraamminecopper(II) ion) exhibits a deep blue color due to the change in the crystal field splitting energy caused by the stronger $\mathrm{NH}_3$ ligands.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{Cu}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_4\right]^{2+}$ is labile complex and changes to $\left[\mathrm{Cu}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4\right]^{2+}$ as $\mathrm{NH}_3$ is stronger ligand than $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$

questions.q: Which among the following is diamagnetic?
questions.solution:
In $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]^{2-}$, the oxidation state of Ni is $+2$. The electronic configuration of $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^8$. Since $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$ is a strong field ligand, it causes pairing of electrons in the $3d$ orbitals. The configuration becomes $t_{2g}^6 e_g^2$ (or $d_{xy}^2 d_{yz}^2 d_{zx}^2 d_{z^2}^2 d_{x^2-y^2}^0$), resulting in zero unpaired electrons, making it diamagnetic.

In $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-}$, Fe is in $+3$ state ($3d^5$). With a strong field ligand, it has one unpaired electron, making it paramagnetic.

In $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{F})_6\right]^{3-}$, Co is in $+3$ state ($3d^6$). F is a weak field ligand, resulting in four unpaired electrons, making it paramagnetic.

In $\left[\mathrm{NiCl}_4\right]^{2-}$, Ni is in $+2$ state ($3d^8$). Cl is a weak field ligand, resulting in two unpaired electrons, making it paramagnetic.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]^{2-}$

questions.q: The complex $\left[\mathrm{PtCl}_2(\mathrm{en})_2\right]^{2+}$ ion shows
questions.solution:
The complex $\left[\mathrm{PtCl}_2(\mathrm{en})_2\right]^{2+}$ has a coordination number of 6, indicating an octahedral geometry. The ligands are two chloride ions and two ethylenediamine (en) molecules, which are bidentate.

The complex can exist in two geometrical forms: the cis-isomer and the trans-isomer. In the trans-isomer, the two chloride ligands are at 180 degrees to each other, resulting in a plane of symmetry, which makes it achiral (optically inactive).

In the cis-isomer, the two chloride ligands are at 90 degrees to each other. The cis-isomer lacks a plane of symmetry and a center of inversion, making it chiral. Therefore, the cis-isomer exists as a pair of enantiomers (optical isomers).

Since the complex exhibits both geometrical isomerism (cis and trans) and optical isomerism (for the cis form), it shows both types of isomerism.

Answer: geometrical and optical isomerism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following complex show optical isomerism?
(i) $c i s-\left[\mathrm{COCl}(\mathrm{en})_2\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)\right]^{2+}$
(ii) $cis-\left[\mathrm{CrCl}_2(\mathrm{ox})_2\right]^{3-}$
(iii) $cis-[ \left.\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{en})_2 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right] \mathrm{Cl}$
(iv) $cis- \left[\mathrm{CO}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right]^{+}$
questions.solution:
Optical isomerism in coordination complexes occurs when the complex lacks a plane of symmetry or center of inversion, making it chiral.

(i) $cis-[CoCl(en)_2(NH_3)]^{2+}$: This complex has two ethylenediamine (en) ligands and two different monodentate ligands. The cis-isomer lacks a plane of symmetry and is optically active.

(ii) $cis-[CrCl_2(ox)_2]^{3-}$: This complex contains two bidentate oxalate (ox) ligands and two chloride ligands in cis positions. It lacks a plane of symmetry and is optically active.

(iii) $cis-[Co(en)_2Cl_2]Cl$: This complex has two bidentate en ligands and two chloride ligands in the cis configuration. It lacks a plane of symmetry and is optically active.

(iv) $cis-[Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2]^{+}$: This complex has a plane of symmetry passing through the two Cl atoms and the Co atom, as well as the plane containing the four $NH_3$ ligands. Therefore, it is achiral and does not show optical isomerism.

Thus, complexes (i), (ii), and (iii) show optical isomerism.

Answer: (i), (ii), (iii)
